q: How is CO2 calculated for a COREX ironmaking unit?
title: COREX ironmaking: CO2 calculation
short: Use a carbon mass balance: carbon in coal, coke and fluxes charged, minus carbon leaving in hot metal, slag and the export gas, times 44/12. The export gas carbon is counted where that gas is burnt, so it must not be counted twice.
audience: Integrated steel plants with COREX smelting reduction units, such as those in the Ballari region of Karnataka

p: COREX gasifies non coking coal with oxygen in a melter gasifier and reduces ore in a shaft above it. It makes a large volume of carbon rich export gas that usually feeds a power plant or a DRI unit.

ul: Inputs: coal, any coke, limestone and dolomite, and electrodes if used.
Outputs: carbon in hot metal, carbon in slag, carbon in export gas sent elsewhere.
CO2 at the unit: (inputs minus outputs) x 44/12.

p: If the gas is burnt in your own power plant, its CO2 sits in your Scope 1 there. If it goes to another company, it leaves your boundary, and the CBAM rules have their own treatment for waste gases exported from steel processes.
